Strategy: 

Always along with a HTF Bias

For Bias I use PXH PXl, Market Maker Models and a top down Analysis 

For Key levels and entries I use Powell’s Model with EL, Key open, Rejection Blocks and FIB

DOL identified before the session always

Minimum RR 1:3, ideal 1:5 on average 

Risk management:
if 1st trade is a win, done for the day
If 1st trade is a loss, I give myself another opportunity with half risk
No matter the outcome for the second trade, I am done for the day

I don’t trade on Bank Holidays, No news Mondays, or before a high impact news release.

I took a small losing trade today trying to short to relative equal lows, but maybe it wasn’t the most amazing setup I could have taken.
,
Market opened higher today and market started off by consolidating for the first portion of new york open until 10:00 where we saw a confusing move down and then up. I saw about 25pts worth of profit before getting stopped out at my trailed stop. We never saw the low taken though and I never found a re-entry. (Screenshot 1)
,
Today was just a mini loss of $165 so I won’t let it deteriorate me from how close I am to passing this account. This kind of thing happens and I am not upset about taking this trade, I just have to carry on and continue to trade like normal.
,

messages.content_text: I know what I did wrong now. My mistake wasn’t the bias or overall read — it was treating the low of the 15m rejection block as true invalidation when, realistically, during NY open on NQ that’s usually just obvious liquidity. My bullish bias still made sense from an AMT/TPO perspective because we had already swept the two single-print highs, still had four single-print lows below, absorption at VAH, and repeated failure to close below the 50% of the RB showing buyers were still defending value. Looking back, the market hadn’t fully finished seeking liquidity yet, and I entered before that process was complete. Since my stop was sitting right below the RB low — where most early longs and RB traders would naturally place stops — the market had incentive to run lower first, clear weak longs, fill larger bids, reset inventory, and then expand higher afterward. That’s why the RB “failed” but the overall thesis still played out and price hit TP later anyway. I also entered a little early because I anticipated the reversal before we got true reclaim/displacement confirming the sweep was complete. The biggest thing I took away from this is understanding the difference between actual structural invalidation and simple liquidity engineering. The higher timeframe idea wasn’t wrong — I just assumed the auction was done seeking liquidity before it actually was.
